% Candidate only. It is not a live-book assertion or a retirement of P21.3.
\begin{proposition}[Invariant toric continuous-pair independence, including boundary]
\label{prop:p213-invariant-toric-boundary-continuous-pairs-candidate}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field, let $N$ be a lattice, let
$\Sigma$ be a rational fan in $N_{\mathbb R}$, and let $X_\Sigma$ be the
associated split toric $K$-variety.  Write
\[
 \operatorname{trop}:X_\Sigma^{\An}\longrightarrow N_\Sigma
\]
for its extended tropicalization.  Let $O\subseteq N_\Sigma$ be open, set
$V=\operatorname{trop}^{-1}(O)$, and let $S$ be the maximal compact torus.
Let $T$ be a positive $\dprime$- and $\ddprime$-closed CLD current of
bidegree $(p,p)$ on $V$, where $0\leq p\leq \dim X_\Sigma-1$.  If $u,v$ are
finite, continuous, $S$-invariant CLD-psh functions on $V$ satisfying
\[
 \dprimeddprime[u]=\dprimeddprime[v],
\]
then
\[
 \dprimeddprime(uT)=\dprimeddprime(vT).
\]
Consequently, every positive closed CLD current on $V$ has the
continuous-pair Bedford--Taylor independence property for finite,
$S$-invariant continuous psh pairs.
\end{proposition}
proof:
% Source-aware verification context for the attached P21.3 subcase only.
\section*{Scope and load-bearing inputs}

The target is a restricted continuous-pair P21.3 assertion on an open inverse
image in a split toric variety.  Unlike the prior dense-torus subcase, its
tropical open set may meet toric boundary strata.  It does not claim the
general P21.3 predicate, noninvariant potentials, nonsplit tori, arbitrary
toroidal charts, or an arbitrary analytic domain.

The proof uses the following precisely delimited inputs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item BGJKK25 equation~(5.5) identifies continuous functions on every open
subset $O\subseteq N_\Sigma$ with $S$-invariant continuous functions on its
analytic inverse image.
\item The test-form calculation in the proof of BGJKK25
Proposition~5.3.10(iv) gives the pushforward identity for the current of a
continuous invariant function.  Its displayed calculation uses factorization,
continuity, canonical-skeleton support of pulled-back top-degree test forms,
and pushforward/differential commutation; it does not use psh positivity.
\item A basic neighborhood of a point in the stratum $N(\sigma)$ has dense
part $\Omega+\sigma$ for open bounded convex $\Omega$.  It contains every
compactified ray in a direction $w\in\sigma$.  This is the neighborhood model
in BGJKK25, proof of Theorem~3.1.4.  On its dense convex part, zero
$\dprimeddprime$ current means an affine continuous representative.  Finite
continuity at all ray endpoints forces its linear functional to vanish on
$\sigma$.
\item In BGJKK25 \S3.3, smooth functions on a tropical toric partial
compactification are exactly the locally smooth functions constant towards
the boundary.  The preceding slope calculation therefore makes the descended
affine function smooth.  BGJKK25 Proposition~2.3.4 pulls smooth Lagerberg
forms back to smooth CLD forms and commutes with both differentials.
\item Finally, the live-book corollary \cref{cor:ch16-smooth-h} says that a
smooth zero-Hessian difference annihilates $\dprimeddprime((u-v)T)$ for any
positive closed CLD current in the displayed bidegrees.
\end{enumerate}

Please reject the candidate if: the pushforward calculation has an omitted
psh or support hypothesis; a basic boundary neighborhood does not supply the
claimed compactified rays; finite continuity does not force the normal affine
slopes to vanish; tropical smoothness fails to pull back to CLD smoothness;
or the final product rule has a bidegree restriction not stated here.

% Candidate only. The cited source statements and live-book interfaces are
% listed explicitly in SOURCE_LEDGER.md.
\begin{proof}
By the invariant-function correspondence (5.5) of \cite{BGJKK25}, there
are unique finite continuous functions $\varphi,\psi$ on $O$ such that
\[
 u=\varphi\circ\operatorname{trop},\qquad
 v=\psi\circ\operatorname{trop}.
\]
The test-form calculation in the proof of Proposition~5.3.10(iv) of
\cite{BGJKK25} uses only this factorization and continuity.  It gives
\[
 [\varphi]=\operatorname{trop}_*[u],\qquad
 [\psi]=\operatorname{trop}_*[v],
\]
and the pushforward commutes with $\dprimeddprime$.  Hence, for
$h:=\varphi-\psi$,
\[
 \dprimeddprime[h]=0\quad\hbox{on }O.
\tag{*}\label{eq:p213-toric-boundary-zero-hessian}
\]

We prove that $h$ is locally smooth with zero Hessian on the tropical toric
partial compactification.  Fix $x\in O$, let $\sigma\in\Sigma$ be the
unique cone with $x\in N(\sigma)$, and choose a basic neighborhood
$W=U(\sigma,\Omega,x_0)\Subset O$, where $\Omega\subset N_{\mathbb R}$
is open, bounded, and convex.  Its dense part $W\cap N_{\mathbb R}$ is the
open convex set $\Omega+\sigma$.  Restricting (*) to this dense part shows,
by the distributional calculation for all second partial derivatives, that
\[
 h(y)=\ell(y)+c\qquad(y\in\Omega+\sigma)
\]
for an affine functional $\ell+c$.

For $y\in W\cap N_{\mathbb R}$ and $w\in\sigma$, the entire compactified
ray $[y,y+\infty w]$ lies in $W$.  Continuity of $h$ at its finite endpoint
therefore makes $\ell(y+tw)+c$ converge as $t\to\infty$.  Thus
$\ell(w)=0$ for every $w\in\sigma$.  The affine function descends through
$N_{\mathbb R}\to N(\sigma)$, and continuity plus density show that on $W$
the function $h$ is exactly that descended affine function.  Equivalently,
$h$ is constant towards every boundary face of $W$ and is smooth for the
standard Lagerberg structure.  Its $\dprimeddprime$ is zero as a smooth
form.

Proposition~2.3.4 of \cite{BGJKK25} pulls this smooth tropical function
back to a smooth CLD function $h\circ\operatorname{trop}$ on
$\operatorname{trop}^{-1}(W)$ and commutes with $\dprimeddprime$.  Since
$u-v=h\circ\operatorname{trop}$, it is locally CLD-smooth with zero
Hessian.  The smooth zero-Hessian product rule
\cref{cor:ch16-smooth-h} now gives
\[
 \dprimeddprime\bigl((u-v)T\bigr)=0.
\]
Linearity of multiplication by $T$ proves the assertion.
\end{proof}
